RAA Masterclass ALICE · heavy-ion collisions
Charged-particle steps (2–5) use the same real ALICE data as the Jupyter notebook (118,909 Pb–Pb collisions recorded by ALICE in 2010 at √sNN = 2.76 TeV, with 38,042,122 charged-particle tracks, and the measured 2.76 TeV pp reference spectrum with its bin-by-bin uncertainties of about 6–10%): every count, yield, RAA and RCP and its uncertainty is computed the way the notebook computes it, with ALICE’s Glauber ⟨Ncoll⟩ values. These RAA and RCP values are for all charged particles together, not for one particle species. The J/ψ steps follow the manual of the official ALICE J/ψ masterclass and contain every recorded collision of its two event files (3,865 pp collisions at √s = 7 TeV and 2,366 p–Pb collisions); the analysis is a copy of the masterclass program’s own (masterclass.C) running in your browser. The extra RpPb step uses ⟨Ncoll⟩ = 6.9 ± 0.7 and compares with ALICE’s published value (JHEP 11 (2015) 127). Masterclass samples are small, pre-selected and not corrected for detector efficiency, so the numbers illustrate the method rather than reproduce ALICE’s publications.
